title: Nintendo Gave Away Fire Emblem for Free to Say Sorry for the 3DS
hook:
In 2011 Nintendo cut the 3DS price by $80 less than six months after launch, then handed early buyers 20 free games, including Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones, which it said it had no plans to sell to anyone else. Were you a 3DS Ambassador?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Nintendo once gave away a Fire Emblem game for free as an apology? The Nintendo 3DS had a slow start in two thousand eleven, and the weak sales numbers worried the company. So on July twenty eighth, less than six months after launch, Nintendo announced an eighty dollar price cut. That was almost a third off the original price. Company president Satoru Iwata wrote an open letter admitting early buyers might feel betrayed. He also cut his own pay in half. To make it right, anyone who connected their 3DS to the eShop before August twelfth became an Ambassador. Ambassadors got twenty free games: ten NES classics and ten Game Boy Advance titles. The GBA batch arrived on December sixteenth, and it included Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones, alongside Metroid Fusion, Minish Cap and Mario Kart Super Circuit. Here is the strange part. Nintendo said it had no plans to sell those ten GBA games to anyone else on the eShop. So the way to get Sacred Stones on a 3DS was to have been stung by the price cut first. An apology gift turned into a members only library. Were you a 3DS Ambassador, and which of the twenty games did you play first? Follow for more gaming history.
